note: Permanent evaluation set. Changing a prompt after metrics collection begins invalidates cross-run comparison (generation success rate, RAG vs no-RAG delta). Add new prompts under a new version instead of editing these.

prompts.prompt: I want an API to manage my personal book collection. Each book has a title, an author, the year it was published, and a list of genres. I should be able to add books, list them, update them, and delete them.
Build me a to-do list API. A task has a title, an optional description, a flag for whether it is done, a due date, and a priority number from 1 to 5.
Create a notes app backend where I can save notes with a title, some body text, and tags. I also want to see when each note was created.
I run a small shop and need an API to track products. For each product I want the name, the price, how many I have in stock, and whether it is currently available for sale.
I need something to keep track of my spending. Every expense should record how much I spent, what category it falls under like food or transport, the date it happened, and an optional note.
I need an API to track my gym workouts.
prompts.tests: Deliberately underspecified. Exercises the PM Agent's rule to resolve vagueness with sensible defaults instead of asking questions, and to populate out_of_scope.

prompts.prompt: Build a contacts API. Each contact has a name, an email address, and a phone number, and belongs to a group such as Family or Work. I want to manage both the contacts and the groups.
I want an API for a small library that stores authors and the books they wrote. An author has a name and a country. A book has a title, the year it was published, and a reference to its author.
Create a blogging backend. A post has a title, body text, and a publish date. Readers can leave comments on a post, and each comment records the commenter's name and their message.

I organise meetups and need an API for events and the people attending them. An event has a name, a location, a date, and a maximum capacity. An attendee has a name, an email, and the event they signed up for.
